final_recommendation: The room converged on a Friday auto-signature deadline with 75% RVC and labor enforcement locked in, conditional on a written 30-day trilateral schedule for Chapter 19 negotiations. Canada's signature depends on that written commitment; without it, the deal stalls despite auto-package consensus.
minority_objections: USTR initially offered only 'best effort' on Chapter 19 without written guarantees, which Congress, labor, and auto industry rejected as insufficient for ratification
Supply-chain manufacturer raised sunset clause uncertainty (hard termination vs. review mechanism) but this was not resolved in the meeting
key_conflicts: Canada refused to sign auto rules without written Chapter 19 commitment, viewing it as betting the farm on good faith
USTR's initial 'best effort' Chapter 19 language vs. stakeholder demand for written 30-day trilateral schedule with dedicated resources
Tension between locking in auto rules Friday vs. ensuring Chapter 19 doesn't collapse immediately after
key_concessions: USTR moved from bilateral-first pressure to accepting parallel Chapter 19 negotiations with written schedule
Canada agreed to Friday auto signature conditional on written Chapter 19 commitment (from initial refusal to sign anything not trilaterally negotiated)
Mexico aligned with Canada on Chapter 19 guarantees rather than pushing for immediate bilateral closure
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain on table as co-equal negotiation with written commitment
Canada: Supply management (dairy) off the table
Labor union: Labor enforcement cannot be hostage to Chapter 19/dairy closure
Congress: No ratification without credible labor enforcement win and forward motion on package
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause mechanism (hard termination vs. review) raised by supply-chain manufacturer but not resolved
Dairy market access linkage proposed but not integrated into final Friday deadline structure
What happens if Chapter 19 negotiations fail after 30 days despite written commitment
downstream_risk_variables: Whether written Chapter 19 commitment materializes by Friday
Whether 30-day Chapter 19 negotiation actually closes or stalls
Sunset clause final language (review vs. hard termination)
Dairy market access terms if auto moves forward without resolution
Supply-chain compliance costs and phase-in adequacy (18-month minimum requested but not confirmed in text)
uncertainty_notes: Sunset clause language unresolved (hard termination vs. review mechanism). Dairy market access proposed but not integrated into Friday deadline. Chapter 19 written commitment format and enforcement mechanism not specified. Phase-in period for auto suppliers (18-month request) not confirmed in final text.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and labor-value-content floor drove the entire Friday signature deadline structure; auto industry demanded phase-in and clear definitions as condition to stop blocking trilateral signature
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress stated 'labor enforcement with real teeth is what my members need to see' and made it the credible win required to hold ratification line; labor union made enforcement non-hostage to Chapter 19 a ratification survival condition
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada declared supply management 'off the table' as red line; dairy rep proposed phased market access but it did not alter the Friday auto-signature structure or become a blocking issue in this meeting
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada refused to sign auto without written Chapter 19 commitment, stating 'if dispute settlement disappears, my government can't defend this deal at home'; drove the written 30-day trilateral schedule demand
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain manufacturer raised sunset uncertainty (hard termination vs. review mechanism) as investment-certainty problem, but it was acknowledged and set aside rather than driving a concrete compromise in this meeting
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'package 90% done but hung up on dispute settlement won't survive ratification pressure' and demanded forward motion; labor union said 'best effort kills this deal' for ratification; drove written Chapter 19 schedule requirement
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry demanded 18-month phase-in for suppliers to retool and clear labor-value definitions to avoid re-sourcing chaos; supply-chain manufacturer raised compliance cost concerns but these were noted rather than driving specific concessions
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's opening ultimatum forced Canada to 'accept the U.S.-Mexico auto package or face bilateral exclusion'; this bilateral-first structure drove Canada's conditional Friday signature and Chapter 19 written-commitment demand

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
